_about: Local models and model failover, the same in both SDKs (2026-09-26, gap-closure plan items 2.8 and 2.4; lane w2-ops).

base_url: the agent-file key a model skill's endpoint is set with (`- openai: {base_url: ...}`), the config key each SDK's skill reads it as, and the environment variable that stands in when the file names none. Until 2026-09-26 the TypeScript loader mapped the key to `baseUrl` while OpenAISkill read `baseURL`, so only OPENAI_BASE_URL worked.

ollama: the provider row of the registry (`skills/llm/providers.ts`, `llm/providers.py`): reached at OLLAMA_BASE_URL through Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, no key (the client is given `placeholder_key`, which Ollama ignores). credential `none` is a server on this machine: never offered as a key, never chosen when the file names no model, listed by `webagents models` with `models_row` and `ready` when it answers (`models_footnote` is the last-but-one line). `status_route` is the chat's /status Model row for a direct Ollama model. `doctor` is the model check when the agent's model is ollama/<model>: the words when it answers and serves the model, when it answers but the model is not pulled, and when nothing answers. `model_match` says when a served id (GET /models) counts as the wanted model: exact, or the wanted name with no tag against the served name's part before the colon.

failover: the agent-file key (a list of provider/model strings; anything else is refused with `invalid`), what the chat says when it moves to the next model (`note`, a warning line in the transcript before the next model's reply), and which failures move on: `retryable` HTTP statuses and a request that never got an answer (`network`); every other failure is reported as it is. A model that had already started answering is never retried (the reply would repeat). `reason` is how each failure is named inside the note. `reason.network` names the origin only to the owner at the terminal (the chat, `webagents -p`); a caller of a served agent reads `reason.network_served`, because an upstream address has no business in a reply (S-228).

cases: run through both SDKs against a stub OpenAI-compatible server on loopback (never a real Ollama or a real key): `requests` is the order of models the server must see, `answered_by` the chain label (provider/model) whose reply came back, `notes` the failover notes said in order (with {port} filled).

ollama.models_footnote: "ready" means this machine has its key: set in this shell, or stored with `webagents secrets set`; for ollama, that it answers at OLLAMA_BASE_URL.

not_pulled.detail: {model}, at {base_url}, but the model is not pulled

unreachable.fix: Start Ollama (`ollama serve`) and pull the model (`ollama pull {bare}`), or set OLLAMA_BASE_URL

failover.invalid: fallback_models: must be a list of provider/model strings

cases.case: the primary answers 503; the fallback answers
notes: openai/primary-model did not answer (HTTP 503); trying openai/fallback-model
openai/primary-model did not answer (HTTP 429); trying openai/fallback-model

cases.case: a bad request is not a provider outage: no failover, the error stands
the primary answers: the fallback is never asked
every model fails: the last failure is reported
notes: openai/primary-model did not answer (HTTP 503); trying openai/fallback-model
